# HD pet art (source images)

Two sets of transparent PNGs, one image per evolution stage:

| file | size | cut for |
|------|------|---------|
| `asset_<stage>.png`     | 200x200 | every panel up to the 240x240 round one |
| `asset_<stage>_400.png` | 400x400 | the 480x480 round panel (LilyGo T-RGB) |

These are the HD remaster of the `src/ui/sprites.h` pixel art: same silhouettes
and palette, redrawn with shading, detail and neon bloom, supersampled then
downscaled.

**Provenance:** generated by a sprite generator in a sibling firmware project,
which draws them procedurally with Pillow and also uses them on a smartwatch
target (loaded from SD as `/HexHound/<stage>.png`). The generator
is the editable source; these PNGs are its committed output. To change a stage,
edit its function in that generator, re-run it, and copy the new
`asset_<stage>.png` here.

**Why two sets, and why the 400 one is not an upscale:** the generator draws on
a 960x960 supersampled canvas and downsamples once at the very end, so the
output size is a knob, not a ceiling. Its `--asset-size` argument sets that
final edge; it defaults to 200, so a plain run reproduces the historic set
byte-for-byte. The 400 set was produced with:

    python tools/gen_hexhound_sprites.py --asset-size 400

and lands in `tools/hexhound_out/asset_<stage>_400.png` (the size is appended to
the filename whenever it is not the 200 default, so the two sets never overwrite
each other). Copy those five files here. Enlarging the 200px set instead would
have given the 480 panel a 2x nearest-neighbour smear; this gives it detail that
was always on the canvas and had simply been thrown away.

**How they reach the firmware:** HexHound has no PNG decoder and no guaranteed
SD card, so `scripts/gen_hd_sprites.py` converts these into RGB565 arrays baked
into flash. One header per panel family, each naming the master it is cut from:

| header | sizes | source |
|--------|-------|--------|
| `src/ui/sprites_hd_small.h`    | 24 + 48   | 200px |
| `src/ui/sprites_hd_big.h`      | 64 + 112  | 200px |
| `src/ui/sprites_hd_round.h`    | 88 + 160  | 200px |
| `src/ui/sprites_hd_round480.h` | 176 + 320 | 400px |

Re-run that script after replacing any PNG here:

    python scripts/gen_hd_sprites.py

The pixel sprites in `src/ui/sprites.h` are still the source of all *animation*
(idle/scan/happy/hungry/alert/hatch/type/laugh). The HD art covers the resting
pet and the evolution hero shot only.
